description: Open-source, local-first desktop AI research workbench for scientific computing with Python/R, MCP bioinformatics tools, SSH/WSL/GPU runtimes, and OpenAI/Anthropic models.
vibe: Ships durable abstractions one small PR at a time, and never runs a test without asking first.
highlights: Durable product nouns (Project, ExecutionContext, DataAsset, Run, Artifact, Paper, Decision) are treated as the control plane, not incidental UI state.
Tests must never depend on real SSH hosts, GPUs, SLURM, WSL, API keys, or network — fakes, temp dirs, and mocked Tauri commands only.
Secrets live in the keyring, never SQLite; SSH private key contents must never be copied into the database.
Model context/output ceilings come from exact model-ID matching in the baked models.dev catalog — prefix/family matching is explicitly banned.
Module splitting is forbidden unless tied to a concrete, measured problem; large composition roots are acceptable and line-count targets are not.
assessment: This file reads like a senior systems engineer's contract with future contributors: it names the durable abstractions, forbids the tempting shortcuts (extending shell timeouts, syncing large data locally, prefix-matching model IDs), and enforces a strict test-permission protocol that prevents agents from burning CI or local resources unprompted. The Escape-stack and shared-icon rules show unusually precise UI discipline for an agent file, and the release section encodes a real operational lesson (create the GitHub Release before CI uploads installers) rather than generic advice. The result is a rare combination of product-level vision and low-level guardrails that keeps an AI agent from drifting into speculative refactors or sloppy cross-boundary serde copies.
